- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; add 1–2 days of upward correction.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative; add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.27” or “0.53” patterns, model tends to underestimate; apply +0.5–1.0% bias to forecast.
